# restate_cloud_byok_registration_key (Resource)

The one-use key that registers a BYOK region: a Restate region that runs in a Kubernetes cluster you build yourself. The BYOC Helm chart's region installation operator presents the key to Restate Cloud, which creates the region under the id the key reserved. Give `key` to the chart as its registration Secret and `region_id` as `region.id`.

A key works once and expires four hours after it is created, so create it after the cluster exists and install the chart soon after. A key that expired or was used is not renewed: replace the resource (`terraform apply -replace=...`) to mint a new one, which reserves a new region id. Every key that no region has used counts against an account limit until it expires.

The API has no operation that reads a key back, so a refresh keeps the state as it is, and the key cannot be imported. Changing any argument other than `deregister_region_on_destroy` replaces the key. The key stays in the Terraform state, as every secret this provider stores does, and is useless there once a region has registered with it or it has expired.

Destroying the resource does not revoke an unused key, because the API cannot, and it leaves the registered region in place unless `deregister_region_on_destroy` is set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The key that registers a BYOK region, which runs in a GKE cluster you build. Create it after the
# cluster exists: it works once and expires four hours after it is created.
resource "restate_cloud_byok_registration_key" "production_us" {
  cloud           = "gcp"
  provider_region = "us-central1"

  # Remove the region at Restate when this resource is destroyed. Restate refuses while the region
  # hosts environments, and the destroy then stops until they are deleted.
  deregister_region_on_destroy = true
}

# The BYOC chart reads the key from a Secret in its release namespace, and takes the region id as a
# value. The gcp-byok module in modules/byoc does both.
output "byok_region_id" {
  value = restate_cloud_byok_registration_key.production_us.region_id
}

output "byok_registration_key" {
  value     = restate_cloud_byok_registration_key.production_us.key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud` (String) Cloud the region's cluster runs on. Only `gcp` is supported.
- `provider_region` (String) The cloud's own name for where the cluster runs, for example `us-central1`. The region must report the same name when it registers, and the chart takes it as `region.providerRegion`.

### Optional

- `deregister_region_on_destroy` (Boolean) When true, destroying this resource also removes the region that registered with the key (`DeleteByokRegion`), which revokes the region's access keys and removes its Restate-side access to the cluster. Restate refuses while the region hosts environments, and the destroy then fails until they are deleted. Defaults to false, which leaves the region registered. A replacement of the key destroys the old resource, so with this set it also removes the region the old key registered. A key that no region has used reserved no region, and there is nothing to remove.
- `region_display_name` (String) The name the Restate Cloud console shows for the region. Restate chooses one when it is omitted.

### Read-Only

- `account_id` (String) Account the key and its region belong to.
- `expires_at` (String) When the key stops working if no region has used it.
- `id` (String) The id of the region the key reserves, the same as `region_id`.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The registration key, for the BYOC chart's registration Secret under the key `key`. Restate shows it only in the response that creates it.
- `region_id` (String) The id the key gives the region it registers, for example `rgn_a1b2c3d4e5`. The chart takes it as `region.id` and derives the region's addresses from it. The region exists at Restate only after the chart has registered.

## Import

This resource cannot be imported. The API shows a registration key once, in the response that creates it, and has no operation that reads one back.
